title.narrative: Morocco Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option

description.narrative: The development objective of the Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option Project for Morocco is to support the Government of Morocco (GoM) in: (a) strengthening the country's institutional capacity to deal with the adverse financial impacts of disasters and climate-related shocks, and (b) strengthening Morocco's institutional framework for disaster and climate-related risk management. This operation builds on a longstanding World Bank engagement with the GoM in disaster risk management (DRM) and disaster risk finance (DRF). Morocco is one of the countries most exposed to geological and climate-related hazards in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. The GoM has developed a strong, cross-sectoral DRM and climate change adaptation policy framework over the last two decades. The framework still suffers from insufficient inter-ministerial coordination of DRM policies and programs, which can jeopardize the progress achieved so far. The linkages and coordination mechanisms between the central and local government layers also lack clarity. Disaster risk information is not systematically generated and shared, which reduces the ability of decision makers in various sectors to use it to inform the design of their programs. The government's recent reforms on catastrophe risk insurance are an important step towards building the country's financial protection against natural catastrophes.

The development objective of the proposed operation is to support the Government of Morocco in (a) strengthening the country's institutional capacity to deal with the adverse financial impacts of disasters and climate-related shocks, and (b) strengthening Morocco's institutional framework for disaster and climate-related risk management.

title.narrative: Number of provinces covered by an integrated flood risk management information system.

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The integrated flood risk management information system has been deployed in June 2023, covering four pilot zones in four provinces. According to DGRN, during the period July 2023 - June 2024, the system was able to issue occasional alerts in the form of a flood risk analysis reports for a number of hydro-meteorological events that could potentially cause flooding.</p>

title.narrative: Share of local officials of the Ministry of Interior responsible for the administration of the register trained on the registration procedures.

comment.narrative: <p>Not achieved. MoI, through a Circular sent to governors of prefectures, provinces, and districts, requested the designation of representatives as focal points responsible for managing the registration of disaster victims. 83 focal points have been designated nationwide and are expected to be trained based on the online registration platform, the registration guidelines, and the user manual on compensation claims processing. Initially planned for September 2023, the training was postponed due to the earthquake and eventally held in November 2023 for the six focal points and 100 data entry agents responsible for the registration of victims in the affected provinces. A training for the remaining focal points will be held in 2024, capturing lessons learned from the earthquake experience.</p>

title.narrative: Number of Civil Protection search and rescue units applying operational and staffing procedures in line with INSARAG standards

comment.narrative: <p>Delayed. Reclassification, on which the standards training depended, has been delayed until 2025 due to the unavailability of INSARAG to physically conduct the exercises. In the meantime, CP conducted core unit training and simulation exercises in line with INSARAG standards with its national search and rescue unit (1 unit of 80 people) and representatives from the 12 regional mobile units (20 people from the 12 units).</p>

title.narrative: Availability of an audit of the FSECs internal control systems confirming that the FSECs systems and procedures allow for the appropriate use of funds.

comment.narrative: <p>Postponed. The audit, a one-time activity initially planned for 2023, was postponed during implementation until 2024 to capture 2023, a significant year for FSEC in terms of staffing and operations, including the earthquake response with the mobilization of US$ 300 million. A dedicated budget was approved in March 2024 and allocated to hire the auditing firm, and the procurement process is set to formally start the week of June 10th with the publication of the request for proposal. The activity is expected to start in September 2024.</p>

title.narrative: Insurance companies comply with the prudential requirements established by the circular.

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The circular, mandating prudential requirements for the accumulation of provisions that can be mobilized in case of severe disasters, was published in March 2020 with immediate effect. The regulatory annual reporting shows MAD 112.56 million for direct businesses in 2022 (MAD 84.88 million in 2021) and MAD 90.86 million for reinsurances’ acceptance in 2022 (MAD 58.65 million in 2021).</p>

title.narrative: Percentage increase in the number of female staff members in the Civil Protection

comment.narrative: <p>Overachieved. As of March 2023, Civil Protection employs 405 female staff, an 11 percent increase from the baseline (364 female civil protection staff members in November 2019).</p>

title.narrative: Annual revenues from the new parafiscal tax created to finance the FSEC.

comment.narrative: <p>Overachieved. The collected parafiscal charge revenues were MAD 197 million in 2020, MAD 230 million in 2021, MAD 243 million in 2022, and MAD 255 million in 2023, exceeding the target set for annual revenue of MAD 200 million (for 2023).</p>

title.narrative: The Government has developed a specific outreach and communication mechanism to inform the population of the registration procedures for people affected by a catastrophic event, with a focus on women.

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. FSEC has a validated communication strategy regarding compensation procedures, a guide and a dedicated website. The outreach strategy includes an in-person caravan with female agents that would physically access remote areas with potential victims.</p>

title.narrative: The Government has deployed an online platform for the registration of people affected by a catastrophic event.

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The first version of the online platform was made operational in 2023 and was successfully deployed after the earthquake.</p>
